title: Islands as connections
paragraphs: The numerous islands of the southern and western seas can be understood as stepping stones rather than isolated fragments. Their significance varied across centuries: some offered shelter for boats, others supplied food or timber, and some became strategic points along coastal routes. Maritime mobility created possibilities for exchanges between the peninsula, the Chinese mainland, and the Japanese archipelago, but winds, currents, and storms always shaped what was feasible.

It would be misleading to picture all voyages as long expeditions by powerful states. Much movement was local, seasonal, or commercial. Short crossings connected households and markets as well as courts. As political authorities expanded, they sought to tax, secure, and sometimes control these routes. The sea could support central power while also providing refuge for people escaping it.
